prompt:
You are reviewing code, not writing it. Do not edit any file.

Review `check_finding`, `check_routing` and the new `trends` parameter of `verify` (and the private helpers they use) in `src/coresight/verify.py` for correctness. Another Muse Code session wrote them against the tests in `tests/test_verify_milestones.py`, and all tests pass, as do the older tests in `tests/test_verify.py`. Your job is to find what the tests do not catch.

Context:
- CoreSight turns photos of drill core trays into a geotechnical log reviewed by a geologist. When a box is approved, a hole agent (an LLM) reads trends that code found between boxes of the drill hole (`hole.hole_trends` in `src/coresight/hole.py`) and proposes one action. Then an orchestrator (an LLM) decides which areas of the mine the box concerns. `check_finding` and `check_routing` are the deterministic checks at those two milestones; a failed check's detail goes back to the model as feedback, at most three attempts, then a person decides. `verify` checks every area draft afterwards.
- Read in this order: the docstring of `tests/test_verify_milestones.py` (the rules), `src/coresight/verify.py`, then in `src/coresight/schemas.py` the classes `HoleTrend`, `RoutingSignals`, `HoleFinding`, `AreaRoute`, `Routing`, `Check`, and in `src/coresight/hole.py` the functions `hole_trends` and `routing_signals` (what the checks receive in production). Then the tests.

Look for:
1. A routing the rules should refuse that passes, or one they should accept that fails: thresholds at exactly 25 and 75, a routing with a route missing or repeated, finance when the lab route is missing, a trend of a kind that should not count.
2. A finding check that can be fooled: an action that passes without the trend it needs, a cited trend that code did not find, a number in the text no tool gave that still passes (for example a year, a depth rounded differently, a number glued to a unit, a negative sign, a percent), or a number that comes from the trends and still fails.
3. Anything in `verify`'s numbers check that changed for drafts without trends (it must behave exactly as before).
4. Details that are not clear sentences, use field names, or would mislead the model that reads them as feedback.
5. Anything that raises where it should not.

For each finding give: the function and line, a concrete input, what the code returns, what it should return and why (cite the rule in the docstring). Say how sure you are. If something is a design choice the docstring states, it is not a bug.

Rules:
- Read only. Do not edit, create or delete any file. Do not run git.
- Do not read or print `.env` or anything under `data/cache` or `data/reviews`. Do not make network calls.
- If you cannot run Python, reason from the code and say so.

Reply with: a one-line verdict (no real errors / real errors found), then the findings, most severe first.

final_answer:
real errors found — 2 foolable number cases in `check_finding`, plus 2 low-severity feedback nits. I could not run Python (sandbox unavailable: `windows_elevated setup_required`), so all below is from reading code.

**1. Negative sign stripped, `-2` passes via `2` — severe, high confidence**

Function: [_check_finding_numbers](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:285) via [_extract_numbers_pct](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:246) and [_NUMBER](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:20).

Concrete input: test box DDH-1 box 3 (runs 10–11, 11–12.5), `history=[]`, `trends=[DROP]`, finding `title="RQD drop"`, `body="RQD falls from 92.4 % in box 2 to 69.3 % in box 3, run 2 at 56.7 %. Level -2 m."`, `trends=["rqd_drop"]`, `action="warn_geotech"`.

What code returns: `numbers ok=True`. `_NUMBER = r"\d+..."` has no sign, so `"-2"` extracts as `raw="2", val=2.0`, which matches box 2 / run 2 / `natural_fractures=2` in [_finding_candidates](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:273).

What it should return: `ok=False` listing the bad number. Rule: [tests/test_verify_milestones.py](D:\Repos\coresight\tests\test_verify_milestones.py:13) “every number in the title and body comes from a tool: the runs … box numbers … and every number of the trends”. No tool gives `-2` (all depths/counts/RQDs `>=0`). Sure: ~90% — sign is part of the number; same regex is used by `verify`, but there it is legacy behaviour that must stay.

**2. `12.5 percent` (word) passes while `12.5 %` (symbol) fails — medium, medium-high confidence**

Function: [_extract_numbers_pct](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:256): `is_pct = text[m.end():].lstrip().startswith("%")`.

Concrete input: same box, `trends=[ZONE]` (weak zone, RQD 41.2/33.8, depths 11.00/13.00; box depth 12.5 exists only as `to_m`, not as RQD), finding `body="RQD 12.5 percent then 41.2 %"`, `trends=["weak_zone"]`.

What code returns: `numbers ok=True`. `12.5` before `" percent"` has `is_pct=False`, checked against all candidates, matches depth `12.5`.

What it should return: `ok=False` with `12.5` in detail, exactly as `test_numbers_in_a_finding_come_from_the_trends_or_the_runs` requires for `"RQD 12.5 % then 41.2 %"` (12.5 m is not 12.5 %). Rule: docstring [13-17](D:\Repos\coresight\tests\test_verify_milestones.py:13) plus that test proving `%`-numbers must match percent tools (`_percent_numbers`). `"percent"/"pct"/"per cent"` is the same quantity in words and bypasses the check. Sure: ~75% — docstring never mentions percents, but the code+test establish the `%` intent; word form is an inconsistent hole.

**3. Second unknown-trend sentence starts lowercase — low, medium confidence**

Function: [_check_finding_trends](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:213), line 220 `detail[0].upper()+detail[1:]`.

Concrete input: `trends=[DROP]`, `finding.trends=["weak_zone","lithology_change"]`.

What code returns: `"Code did not find a weak zone along the hole; code did not find a change of rock along the hole"` (second `code` lowercase).

What it should return: both clauses capitalised as sentences. Rule: docstring [18-19](D:\Repos\coresight\tests\test_verify_milestones.py:18) “Failed details are sentences without field names”. Sure: ~60% — readable but not sentences; does not mislead.

**4. `finance ok` when `lab` route is missing — low, low confidence**

Function: [_check_finance](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:366) (`if lab_applies is None: return ok`), called from [check_routing](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:378).

Concrete input: `Routing` with `lab` skipped, `finance applies=True`, any `signals`.

What code returns: `lab` fails `"Lab has no route"`, `finance ok=True`.

What it arguably should return: `finance` fail (no lab request to price). Rule: docstring [31](D:\Repos\coresight\tests\test_verify_milestones.py:31) “finance applies exactly when lab applies (it only prices the lab request)”. With no lab route there is no request, so `True` contradicts the rule, paralleling the `"lab does not apply"` cannot-case. Sure: ~40% — docstring [32](D:\Repos\coresight\tests\test_verify_milestones.py:32) only says the missing area fails, overall routing still fails via `lab`, so this may be intended to avoid double-failure; flagging only for clarity.

Checked and found correct (no finding): safety thresholds `<25` / `>=75` at exactly 25/75; `lab/safety/plant` trend-kind filtering (`rqd_drop`/`weak_zone` only for safety, `sulfides_*` only for plant-must, `lithology_change` only allows plant); missing-route `"<Area> has no route"` and `lab,safety,plant,finance` order; duplicated routes impossible via `Routing._one_per_area`; `verify` without `trends` adds `_trend_numbers([])=[]` so behaviour is unchanged; no reachable `raise` (the only `KeyError` path, `_TREND_WORDS[k]`, needs an invalid `TrendKind` that Pydantic rejects before the check).
